entries.name: Maliketh, the Black Blade
entries.content:
Maliketh, the Black Blade is a boss in Elden Ring, encountered in Crumbling Farum Azula. This is not an optional boss as Maliketh must be defeated to unlock Leyndell, Ashen Capital and reach the endgame of Elden Ring.

Overview
Maliketh is the loyal Shadowbound Beast and half-brother of Queen Marika the Eternal,[1][2] an Empyrean of Numen descent,[3] who would become the vessel of the Elden Ring.[4]

Maliketh fought and defeated the Gloam-Eyed Queen, the leader of the Godskin Apostles.[5] On Marika's orders, Maliketh sealed away the Rune of Death,[1] binding it within his blade,[6] causing the true power of the god-slaying black flame to be lost.[7]

When the Rune of Death was plucked from the Elden Ring,[8] and confined,[9] the Golden Order was created, with Queen Marika as its one true god.[10] Marika's offspring were granted a form of immortality owing to the removal of their fated deaths from the Elden Ring,[11] however there was not one Demigod who did not fear Maliketh and his blade imbued with death.[2] He was a beast of such terrifying ferocity that his name came to mean "Death of the Demigods".[12] He also led the Black Blade Kindred, living gargoyles who wielded weapons held together by blackened corpse wax.[13]

During the Golden Age of the Erdtree, a fragment of the Rune of Death was stolen from Maliketh.[14] The perpetrator was Ranni the Witch, who used it to forge godslaying black knives,[15] which were wielded by the Black Knife Assassins during the assassination of Godwyn the Golden on the Night of Black Knives.[16] Maliketh responded by binding his blade- and the Rune of Death sealed within- into his own flesh, to prevent death from ever being stolen again.[6] Later, the Rune of Death sprouted from Godwyn's corpse and began to spread through the Lands Between in the form of Deathroot. Maliketh, under the name Gurranq, resolved to track down and devour the Deathroot,[17] eventually gaining an insatiable hunger for it.[18]

Maliketh, now Gurranq, eventually came into contact with D, Hunter of the Dead. D entered Gurranq's service and assisted him in weeding Deathroot, the source of Those Who Live in Death.[19] D would later find a Tarnished, who agreed to take his place in weeding Deathroot.[20]

The Tarnished encounters Gurranq in the Bestial Sanctum in Caelid. The beast, dressed in the robes of a clergyman, gives them an eye which trembles in the presence of Deathroot,[21] and instructs them to bring him any Deathroot they find in return for bestial incantations.[22] Despite consuming all the Deathroot the Tarnished could bring him, Gurranq is not sated. Despondent, he realises that he has done all he can for the land and departs, with his hunger as his only companion.[23]

When the Tarnished arrives at the foot of the Erdtree, they find the entrance obstructed by thorns. To remove the thorns, the Tarnished and their companion, Melina, set the Erdtree ablaze at the Giant's Forge.[24] After doing so, the Tarnished finds themselves in Crumbling Farum Azula, an ancient city in the sky, where they seek the Rune of Death.[25] The Tarnished finally comes upon Gurranq, who attempts to stop them from stealing the Rune of Death from him.[26] Despite his best efforts, Gurranq struggles to overcome the Tarnished. As a last resort, he unbinds his death-imbued blade from his flesh and reveals his true identity to the Tarnished.[27] Nevertheless, Maliketh falls to the Tarnished, and with his dying breath cries out to Marika for forgiveness.[28] The Rune of Death is unbound, and enshrouds the Lands Between. However, this allows the impenetrable thorns to finally burn away,[29] allowing the Tarnished to finally gain access to the Erdtree.

entries.name: Greater Will
entries.content:
The Greater Will is a mysterious and supremely powerful entity or force from beyond that has great influence over the Lands Between. The vassals and envoys of the Greater Will are central to the Golden Order. It inhabits a lightless void outside the Lands Between.[1]

Background
Long ago, the Greater Will fractured the One Great, creating births and souls.[2] The adherents of the Three Fingers consider this action to be a mistake, because it resulted in torment, despair, affliction, sins, and curses.

Together with a golden star, the Greater Will once sent an Elden Beast to the Lands Between that would later become the Elden Ring.[3] This beast was its vassal, and the living incarnation of the concept of Order.[4] The Greater Will has other vassals and envoys known as the Two Fingers,[5] who speak in a sign language of light.[6]

Eternal Cities
Before the age of the Erdtree,[7] the denizens of the Eternal Cities rebelled against the Greater Will. To shield themselves from its influence, the Nox donned ritual mirrorhelms to block its intervention and that of its vassals.[8] In an act of blasphemy, they drew the ire of the Greater Will by wielding the Fingerslayer Blade against one of its vassals.[9] In response to this transgression, the Greater Will unleashed Astel, whose destruction of the Eternal Cities condemned them to an existence underground.[10]

Age of the Erdtree
During the age of the Erdtree begun by Queen Marika the Eternal[11] and at least the era immediately preceding it, the Greater Will's envoy Two Fingers selected Empyreans as candidates to become the God of the coming age.[12] Queen Marika was one such candidate, and created the Golden Order by confining the Rune of Death.[13] However, Marika would eventually shatter the Elden Ring,[14] leading to her demigod offspring inheriting the Great Runes which in turn would trigger a war known as the Shattering.[15] The Greater Will abandoned the demigods following the Shattering, as none managed to claim title of Elden Lord.[16]

According to the Two Fingers, the Greater Will has not abandoned the realm, nor the life that inhabits it, proclaiming this is why the Tarnished have been extended the Guidance of Grace.[17] After the Tarnished returned to the Lands Between following the Shattering, the Two Fingers, at the behest of the Greater Will, bade them kill the demigods in order to claim their Great Runes to become Elden Lord by becoming Marika's consort,[18] as the Greater Will had long since renounced the demigods.[19]

In the time of The Tarnished (Protagonist), it was discovered that the entrance to the Erdtree was blocked by impenetrable thorns, preventing anyone from becoming Elden Lord. This caused the Two Fingers to commune with the Greater Will in search of answers, which may take thousands or tens of thousands of moons.[20][21] When The Tarnished (Protagonist) suggested burning the Erdtree, which would unbind Destined Death and slay the world itself,[22] Finger Reader Enia exclaimed that the Fingers and the Greater Will would never allow it.[23]

After The Tarnished (Protagonist) caused the Volcano Manor's recusants to disband following the defeat of Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, the recusant known as Knight Bernahl declared himself the inheritor of his comrade recusant's will. He declared their refusal to become the Greater Will's pawns and swore it would fall by his blade.[24]

It is often speculated that the Greater Will is an Outer God or equivalent due to its God-like standing in the world of Elden Ring. It is never directly referred to as one in the game's text, however.
The Nox Mirrorhelms presumably worked by reflecting the Greater Will's language of light.[25]

entries.name: Nox
entries.content:
The Nox are the inhabitants of the Eternal Cities of Nokron and Nokstella. They are a grey-skinned, cold-blooded race known for wielding flowing weapons[1] forged from the liquid metal of Silver Tears.

Long ago, the Nox committed treason against the Greater Will and its vassal Fingers, fashioning crystalline helmets out of glass to ward off their intervention.[2] However, they invoked the ire of the Greater Will and were banished deep underground, forced to live under a false night sky in eternal anticipation of the coming age of stars, and of their Lord of Night.[3]

Variant Description
Monks clad in armour with silk capes and hoods. They wield Flowing Hammers which can elongate in a whip-like fashion for additional range, turn into semi-spherical spiked fist weapons which they dual-wield, or into single, spherical weapons resembling censers.

entries.name: Hornsent
entries.content:
The Hornsent were the inhabitants of Belurat and the tower of Enir-Ilim. They associated the spiral and tangled horns with the divine.[1] The hornsent butchered undesirables and stuffed them into jars. They conducted a divine ritual to rebirth the jar contents as better people. The Hornsent performed such rituals with the jars, mixing and amalgamating different people into a formation of flesh and spirit, in a sort of attempt to obtain a higher being through the sacrifice of many beings contained in said jars.

The Hornsent's ambition, through the jars, was to reach beings with the quality of divinity. The pillars and spiral-shaped symbols are the representation of this ambition.

Downfall
Queen Marika betrayed hornsent.[6][7]. Their tower and and its Divine Gate was sealed by shadow[8] and their lands hidden in the Realm of Shadow. The hornsent were later attacked by forces of the Erdtree led by Messmer, son of Marika. His flame burned their armies and settlements.[9][10] Those who survived bore a deep grudge or swore vengeance.[11][12]

entries.name: Ancient Ruins of Rauh
entries.content:
The Ancient Ruins of Rauh, also known as the Rauh Ruins, is a subregion of the Realm of Shadow in Shadow of the Erdtree.

The Ancient Ruins of Rauh are perched above the Rauh Base and connected to the Shadow Keep via a bridge to the east. These ancient ruins are the upper section of the Rauh Ruins, located within the Land of the Tower, adjacent to the towering Enir-Ilim. A small portion of this area can be accessed early through a Sending Gate at the Fifth Belfry, found behind Castle Ensis on the Scadu Altus.

The Rauh Ruins are densely overgrown with vegetation.[1] These remnants are what remains of a long-forgotten civilization that mastered the lost art of sprite magic long before the rise of the hornsent and advent of Marika's Erdtree.[2] A mysterious woman with an octagonal hat is prominently featured in much of the ruin's architecture. The ruins narrowly escaped destruction during Messmer's cleansing Crusade, thanks to the intervention of Fire Knight Salza, who defied orders to burn them.[3]

entries.name: Messmer the Impaler
entries.content:
Messmer the Impaler is a mandatory Remembrance boss in Shadow of the Erdtree. He is a Demigod who is encountered in the Shadow Keep and the source of the Messmer's Flame Incantations.

Messmer was born to Queen Marika the Eternal prior to the Second Liurnian War.[6] His birth was cursed by a dark entity, an evil serpent coiled within that threatened to subsume him.[8] Known to Messmer as the Abyssal Serpent,[9] this force was restrained only through Marika's intervention—she removed her son's right eye and replaced it with a seal of her Grace.[3] Ever since his accursed birth, Messmer was in constant company of the winged serpents, friends who suppressed the base serpent.[5]

Much like his younger sister, Messmer bore a vision of fire.[8] He despised this flame, and time and time again hoped to rid himself of it, but found that it ever burned.[10]

At some point, Messmer befriended Commander Gaius, an Albinauric who like him was cursed from birth. Gaius would go on to command Messmer's armies in the wars to come. They both acted as "older brothers" to General Radahn.[6]

 Crusade
Before the Shattering, Messmer was charged by his mother with carrying out a purge of the tower-dwelling hornsent of the Land of Shadow, who did not bear the light of grace. At some point during his Crusade, Messmer was abandoned in the Land of Shadow, but continued to zealously enforce the purge even though Marika ceased all contact with him. Messmer came to reside in a fort known as the Shadow Keep.

Key in his army were the Black Knights, commanded by Black Knight Commander Andreas and his son and second-in-command Black Knight Captain Huw. Although they remained devoutly loyal to Messmer despite his abandonment by Marika, they ultimately rebelled upon learning of his serpentine nature. The pair were imprisoned in an underground tomb, and despite his betrayal, Messmer mourned the loss of Huw, whom he had considered a brother-in-arms.[11] [12] His Fire Knights rebelled against burning the Ancient Ruins of Rauh and the destruction of the specimens in the Specimen Storehouse.[13][14]

Eventually, an intruder invaded Messmer's stronghold, the Shadow Keep, and was noticed by the demigod's serpents, who identified them as a Tarnished Champion and a pretender to the title of Elden Lord. Though surprised that a Tarnished had come to the Land of Shadow, Messmer nonetheless attacked them to continue enforcing the purge. However, the serpentine demigod struggled overcome the Tarnished. Unwilling to accept "a Lord devoid of light" and desperate to regain the upper hand, Messmer ripped out Marika's seal and unleashed the power of the Abyssal Serpent, allowing him to frequently transform into a massive serpent. Nonetheless, the Tarnished was able to land a fatal blow upon Messmer. Realizing that his mother had indeed forsaken him, Messmer used his dying breath to curse Marika.

Messmer, much like his siblings Malenia and Miquella, was also born cursed. Exactly when he was born remains unknown as all mention of him was erased by his mother after she abandoned him in the Land of Shadow.
Messmer did, however, act as an elder brother to Radahn, who is older than the twins, making Messmer at the very least their older brother.
In one of the item descriptions of Messmer's Kindling it says that "His younger sister also bore a vision of fire", possibly relating to Melina. She serves as kindling to burn the Erdtree, and so too did Messmer have kindling capable of burning a tree.
While unconfirmed, Messmer is implied to be a child of Radagon:
He is red-haired, a trait commonly seen in Radagon's children.
He was born cursed, much like Malenia and Miquella, who were born "from a single god".
There are four butterfly items shown in the game and its expansion: Nascent - Miquella, Aeonian - Malenia, Smouldering - Melina, and Black Pyrefly - Messmer.
Radagon's motif is present in the soundtrack of Messmer's fight.
If Messmer is a child of Marika-Radagon, then he had the potential to rise as an Empyrean.[15]
Upon his defeat, Messmer denounces his mother and curses her with his dying breath.[16] This is the only time he refers to Marika by name.

entries.name: Gideon Ofnir, The All-knowing
entries.content:
Gideon Ofnir is the Tarnished leader of Roundtable Hold and the adoptive father of Nepheli Loux.[1] Called to the Lands Between by the guidance of Grace, Gideon wishes to become Elden Lord.[2] To this end he accumulates information on the Shardbearers, employing a network of spies[3] to aid in his hunt for knowledge. Initially, he is apprehensive of the Tarnished, but after they have claimed a Great Rune he becomes willing to share his knowledge of the remaining shardbearers.

In the past, Gideon took in Nepheli Loux after she lost sight of the guidance of Grace, taking advantage of her youthful credulity.[4] He promised her that he would not allow the downtrodden to be cheated any longer if he became Elden Lord.[5] He also became acquainted with Preceptor Seluvis and Dolores the Sleeping Arrow, although he and Seluvis would go their separate ways because of Dolores.[6]

At some point, Gideon engaged in a long exchange with the Two Fingers, and in doing so learned that everything- including the Erdtree and the Two Fingers themselves- had been broken.[7] He also glimpsed into the will of Queen Marika the Eternal, shuddering in fear at an end that should not be.[8] He concluded from this that the queen wished for the Tarnished to struggle eternally.[9]

When a Tarnished champion makes their way to the Roundtable Hold, the first in a long time, Gideon is initially dismissive of them, welcoming them to the Hold but calling them a mere visitor. Gideon encourages the Tarnished to seek a Great Rune in order to gain audience with the Two Fingers and be welcomed as a proper member of the Roundtable Hold.

True to his word, Gideon inducts them as a true member of the Roundtable upon their meeting with the Two Fingers, and shares with them some of the information he has amassed on the Shardbearers.

Although Gideon had amassed knowledge on many of the shardbearers, he had not ascertained the whereabouts of four demigods: Ranni the Witch; Mohg, Lord of Blood; Malenia, Blade of Miquella; and Miquella of the Haligtree. In his search for the latter, he sends his men to ransack the Village of the Albinaurics in Liurnia of the Lakes, knowing that the Albinaurics possess half of a secret medallion that would open the path to the Haligtree. The slaughter of the Albinaurics causes Nepheli to lose faith in him, which causes him to abandon her.[10] He also sought Latenna, an Albinauric woman with knowledge of the location of the other half of the medallion.[11] If the Tarnished claims one half of the medallion, Gideon's underling Ensha will ambush them in Roundtable Hold, apparently of his own volition.[12] After Ensha is defeated, Gideon compensates the Tarnished by sharing the possible whereabouts of the medallion's other half.

When the Erdtree rejects the Tarnished, forcing them to contemplate journeying to the Forge of the Giants to burn the thorns barring entry into the Erdtree, Gideon encourages them to take no heed of the Fingers' warning that this would be a cardinal sin. He also offers to reward the Tarnished for any information they can deliver on the four great runes whose locations are unknown. If the Tarnished pursues this quest to its ending, finding the cocoon of Miquella within the Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum, Gideon thanks them, declaring that this is one of the last pieces he needs to put everything together.

After the Tarnished burns the Erdtree and unseals the Rune of Death, Gideon makes his way to Leyndell, Ashen Capital, where he confronts the Tarnished in the Erdtree Sanctuary. Upon his defeat, he warns them that a Tarnished could not become a Lord, and that a man cannot kill a god.[13]

Character Information
Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing is a boss encounter in Leyndell, Ashen Capital. He utilises both sorceries and incantations in combat, and learns new spells depending on whether you have defeated Rykard, Malenia, or Mohg. He only has seven memory slots, and knows six spells by default, meaning that the spells learned by defeating the aforementioned bosses can replace his default spells. If two of these bosses have been defeated, Gideon will lose Comet Azur. If all three have been defeated, he will lose Triple Rings of Light.

The Omenkiller in the Village of the Albinaurics is implied by Nepheli to be one of Gideon's agents. Due to the connection between Omenkillers and perfumers, the Depraved Perfumer in the village may be working with the Omenkiller.
Recusant Henricus, an invader in Limgrave, wears the Eye Surcoat which is said to be worn by Gideon's "eyes and ears".
The Eye Surcoat can be looted from a corpse in Rykard's boss arena. This is potentially another agent of Gideon.

entries.name: Nepheli Loux, Warrior
entries.content:
Nepheli Loux is a Tarnished warrior [1]from the Badlands. In her infancy, Nepheli lived through murder and pillage unchecked[2] At some point, she lost the guidance of grace, and was taken in by Gideon Ofnir, who became her foster father.[3] Gideon promised Nepheli that if he became Elden Lord he would never allow the downtrodden to be cheated again[4], earning her loyalty and aid in his pursuit of the title of Elden Lord.[5]

At the behest of Gideon, Nepheli infiltrates Stormveil Castle[6], the home of the demigod Godrick the Grafted. Here, she encounters a Tarnished, who aids her in defeating the decrepit demigod. With Godrick slain, she returns to Roundtable Hold, where she awards them with an Arsenal Charm she found in Stormveil, and encourages them to speak to her foster father.

Travelling to Liurnia of the Lakes, Nepheli comes upon the Village of the Albinaurics, where she witnesses the slaughter of the Albinauric inhabitants at the hands of her father's men.[7] Reminded of the brutality she witnessed as a child, Nepheli vows to deliver justice to the oppressors[8], assisting the Tarnished in defeating the Omenkiller responsible for the slaughter.

For giving into her emotions and abandoning the mission, Nepheli is cast aside by Gideon.[9] Without her estranged father's guidance, she becomes crestfallen, resigning to the lower levels of Roundtable Hold where she questions the faith she had in Gideon.[10]

The Tarnished obtains the ashes of The Stormhawk King in the Chapel of Anticipation, which they may choose to give to Nepheli. She can smell the ancient storm within the ash[11], and is reminded of her first hawk.[12] Despite her inability to sense spirits within ash[13], she gladly receives them.

After claiming the Stormhawk King's ashes, Nepheli encounters Kenneth Haight, who recognises her as a worthy heir of Limgrave.[14] Nepheli accepts the role, having been reminded by Limgrave of her own home.[15] As the new lord of Limgrave, Nepheli pledges to aid the Tarnished should they become Elden Lord[16], pledging to call upon the storm to drive away the foulness that has settled on the winds.[17]

Nepheli Loux's name implies that she is related to Godfrey, who's name following his banishment from the Lands Between is Hoarah Loux. This connection is also supported by Kenneth Haight's decision to appoint her as the new lord of Limgrave, following his proclamation to find someone of the "proper lineage".

entries.name: Roderika, Spirit Tuner
entries.content:
A Tarnished[1] noblewoman who, despite having never seen the guidance of grace[2], travelled to the Lands Between along with her companions. After arriving, those companions fell victim to Godrick, becoming subjects for his grafting.[3] Roderika alone survived, taking refuge in Stormhill Shack. It is here that she meets the Tarnished. She beseeches the Tarnished to bring a message to her grafted companions, whom she refers to as chrysalids, assuring them that she loves them and will join them soon.[4]

Roderika then heads to Roundtable Hold. Here, she becomes acquainted with Smithing Master Hewg, who takes notice of her gift for spirit tuning and is reminded of a spirit tuner he knew long ago, whose eyes were of the same hue as Roderika's.[5] Reluctantly, Hewg agrees to teach Roderika everything he knows about spirit tuning.

Roderika remains at Roundtable Hold, where she hones her newfound talent and eventually becomes a fully-fledged spirit tuner.[6] Her ability to sense spirits allows her to notice the Dung Eater's presence, which she warns the Tarnished about.[7]

After the Erdtree burns, Roderika attempts to convince Hewg to leave Roundtable[8], but to no avail. She chooses to respect Hewg's decision, and remains behind with him even after he forgets her.[9] As the hold burns, she begs the Tarnished to become Elden Lord, and to use the weapons Hewg forged to slay Queen Marika the Eternal.[10]

entries.name: Smithing Master Hewg
entries.content:
Hewg is a prisoner of Roundtable Hold, tasked with smithing weapons for the Tarnished.[1] His duty, given by Queen Marika the Eternal, is to smith a weapon to kill a god.[2][3] In the past, Hewg was indebted to a spirit tuner,[4] and when he meets Roderika he recognises that her eyes share the same hue as those of his old acquaintance.[5] Although reluctant at first, Hewg agrees to take Roderika under his wing at the insistence of the Tarnished.

After the Tarnished sets fire to the Erdtree, the Roundtable Hold also begins to burn. Hewg's chains are broken, yet he insists on remaining in the hold, where he can continue to smith weapons to slay a god, despite Roderika's pleas for him to leave.[6] As the Roundtable burns, Hewg's mental state appears to deteriorate, causing him to slur his words and, eventually, to forget both Roderika and the Tarnished.[7] Roderika decides to respect Hewg's decision to stay at the Roundtable, and resolves to remain with him.[8] Her last request is for the Tarnished to use the weapons Hewg smithed to slay Queen Marika.[9]

entries.name: War Counselor Iji
entries.content:
A good-natured troll who once served the Carian Royal Family as a blacksmith.[1] Currently, Iji serves Ranni, the Carian princess, as her war counsellor,[2] while still plying his trade as a blacksmith outside the Kingsrealm Ruins, near the Caria Manor.

Iji has known Ranni and Blaidd since they were children, and they would let him join in when they played.[3] Along with Blaidd, he swore allegiance to Ranni when she renounced her flesh and chose the dark path of the Empyrean.[4] Iji is also shown to care for Blaidd[5], however he also harbours some reservations. Fearing that, as her sworn shadow, Blaidd will go mad and become a curse for Ranni for resisting the Two Fingers[6], Iji imprisons Blaidd in the Forlorn Hound Evergaol.[7]

Iji became acquainted with Jerren when he was a guest of the Carians.[8] Jerren recalls that the weapons Iji smithed were blunt, yet did not decay when faced with Scarlet Rot.[9] Jerren may also offer a vital clue regarding Ranni's fate, which helps Iji to come to the realisation that General Radahn must be killed in order to release the stars and Ranni's own fate.[10]

Later, after Blaidd breaks free of his imprisonment and gives his life in defence of Ranni, Iji admits that he misjudged Blaidd's loyalty, and senses that he will soon join Blaidd in death.[11] Later, he can be found dead, his body ablaze with black flame, with the corpses of Black Knife Assassins nearby.

entries.name: Primeval Current
entries.content:
The primeval current of glintstone sorcery is intrinsically tied to the cosmic vitality of the stars,[2] shaping both the land and fate of the Lands Between.[3][4] It is described as a torrent of glintstone flowing from a distant star cluster,[5] often likened to a celestial procession of stars.[1]

However, those who gaze into the current are bewitched by its cosmic mysteries, often driven to the brink of despair.[5][6]

Long ago, the Greater Will triggered a great rupture in the One Great,[7][8] scattering the ancient life of the stars across the cosmos.[2] This celestial event is seen as the primordial causality that led to fractures, births, and souls.[9]

An ancient astrologer on the Mountaintops of the Giants perceived the primeval current, giving it form[citation needed] and bringing its amber raining down upon the Lands Between.[10] These celestial phenomena introduced glintstone sorcery and its cosmic vitality into the world.

Many of these shooting stars became meteors that struck the Lands Between, giving rise to the Alabaster and Onyx Lords and lifting Farum Azula into the sky.[11][12][13][14] The first star to arrive carried Metyr, Mother of Fingers, daughter of the Greater Will.[15] Later, a golden star descended, bearing the Elden Beast, which would become the Elden Ring.[16]

The Black Moon once hung over Nokstella, guiding countless stars.[17][18] However, it was lost when the Nox used the Fingerslayer Blade against Metyr,[19][20] enraging the Greater Will.[21] In response, the Greater Will sent Astel, Naturalborn of the Void,[22] to assault the Eternal Cities.[23][24] Astel unleashed a hail of meteorites, destroying the Nameless Eternal City and stealing its night sky,[25] an act that banished the Eternal Cities underground.

The Academy of Raya Lucaria was later founded by two glintstone sorcerers, Azur and Lusat, who sought to uncover the secrets of glintstone and the enigmatic Crystalians. Both peered beyond the "wisdom of stone"[26][27] into the primeval current and were irrevocably changed by what they saw.[28][29] Azur was left bewitched and haunted by the abyss,[5] while Lusat was shattered after witnessing the dying light of a star cluster.[6]

When the Carians, worshippers of the Moon and allies of the crystalians,[30] gained control of the academy,[31][32] they suppressed the study of the primeval current.[33] However, Sorceress Sellen defied this ban, obsessively pursuing its secrets. Operating under the alias of the Graven Witch, she transformed her fellow sorcerers into Graven Masses—the seeds of stars.[34][35] For her treachery, she was expelled from the academy.[36][37]

After the Shattering, a young General Radahn applied the Gravity Sorcery he had learned from an Alabaster Lord in Sellia, Town of Sorcery.[38][39][40] In the ensuing Starscourge Conflict, Radahn stood alone against the stars and triumphed.[41][42] His victory halted the movement of the stars, thereby forestalling the fate of his sister, Ranni.[43]

The Demi-Human Queens task their Demi-Human Swordsman with discovering what lies beyond the procession of the stars.[1][44] Demi-Human Swordmaster Onze sealed himself in the Belurat Gaol to forestall the ruinous fate he perceived.[45]
The Greater Will exists in a lightless abyss, or void, far beyond the Lands Between.[46] It is the home of Astel and the Fallingstar Beasts.[47][48]
It is possible Astel used a wormhole to reach the Eternal Cities.[23][49]
Azur slowly transformed into blue-green glintstone.[28]
Lusat slowly transformed into deep blue glintstone.[29]
Mad Tongue Alberich and the Guilty transform blood sacrifices into red glintstone.[50]

entries.name: Sorceress Sellen
entries.content:
Sellen was considered to be the most promising glintstone sorceress to ever attend the Academy of Raya Lucaria.[1] Her first teacher at the academy was the sorcerer Azur, one of the founding glintstone sorcerers and originator of the Karolos Conspectus.[2][3] Azur, along with Lusat, was banished from the academy due to their study of the primeval current[4], a study Sellen wished to pursue. However, following accusations of unspeakable treatment of her fellow scholars under the name of the Graven Witch, Sellen too was expelled from the academy.[5] Sellen had sought to restore the Primeval Current, desiring glintstone sorceries unbound by terrestrial taboos and the pedantry of the Carian Royal Family.[6]

Sellen was also an acquaintance of Preceptor Seluvis, and a frequent visitor to his underground cellar[7], where he kept his collection of puppets. When Sellen was expelled, Seluvis helped her in some capacity, for which she owes him.[8]

At some point following her banishment, Sellen was imprisoned in Witchbane Ruins on the Weeping Peninsula, bound by the Academy's shackles.[9] She managed to manifest a projection of herself[10] in the Waypoint Ruins in Limgrave. It is here that she meets the Tarnished, who becomes her apprentice[11], learning glintstone sorceries from her. When she learns that the Tarnished has found Master Azur on Mt. Gelmir, she requests that they seek out Master Lusat, speculating that he returned to his home of Sellia, Town of Sorcery.[12] The Tarnished discovers Lusat, in a near-inorganic state[13] much like Azur, in Sellia Hideaway, and reports back to Sellen.

Freeing Sellen
Much like Ranni the Witch, Sellen's fate is tied to the stars, and with the defeat of Starscourge Radahn, Sellen becomes dispossessed of her immortality.[14] This makes her a target of Jerren, a friend of the Carian Royal Family who once made a promise to exterminate the witch. Sellen reveals to the Tarnished that the form they have been speaking to is a projection[10], and that her true body resides in Witchbane Ruins.[15] The Tarnished meets with Sellen's true body, shackled in the ruin's cellar, and she asks them to remove her Primal Glintstone, beseeching them to look after it.[16] Jerren arrives to find Sellen's previous body already perished.[17] The Tarnished later places Sellen's Primal Glintstone into a puppet in Seluvis's basement, which bears a striking resemblance to Sellen's old body.

Sellen, now in her new, more youthful body[18], returns to the Academy and displaces Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon.[19] She has the bodies of Azur and Lusat moved back to the Academy, so that she can finally hone the Primeval Current.[20] She offers her support to the Tarnished in their mission to become Elden Lord, and requests that when the time comes, they illuminate her about the secrets of life which course the Elden Ring[21] Before long, however, Jerren finally catches up to her. [22] Should the Tarnished aid her in beating back Jerren, she will continue her research. When the Tarnished next sees her, she has transformed into a Graven Mass.

Portraits of Sellen are hung around the Academy of Raya Lucaria, notably the Debate Parlor.
Sellen may be summoned as a cooperator against the Red Wolf of Radagon if her Primal Glintstone has been inserted in the doll body from Seluvis's Cellar. Given that this requires both reaching the top of Mt. Gelmir and defeating Starscourge Radahn before you have made significant progress in the Academy of Raya Lucaria, this is rather unlikely to happen naturally.

entries.name: Fire Giant
entries.content:
The Fire Giant is a boss in Elden Ring. He is encountered at Flame Peak on the Mountaintops of the Giants. This encounter is not optional as it must be completed to unlock Crumbling Farum Azula and advance the main storyline.

n the days before the Erdtree, the Giants carved out a civilization in the inhospitable mountains to the north, after chasing away the Ice Dragons who had previously ruled it.[1] Here, they worshipped a Fell God and were bound to tend the Flame of their god for eternity.[2]

Before Queen Marika the Eternal ushered in her Age of the Erdtree, she had her then husband, Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, launch an attack against the Giants,[3] fearing that their fire might burn her Erdtree.[4]

The mighty Giants borrowed the power of their fell god, but were still defeated[2] by Godfrey[5] and his Crucible Knights,[6] with Marika allegedly striking down the fell god.[7] Only a single Fire Giant remained, and Marika cursed him to forever tend his Flame, ensuring it could not harm her Erdtree.[8] During this time, the Fire Giant crafted a leg brace for a wound on his left leg.

After untold ages of tending the flame, the Fire Giant's vigil is interrupted by a Tarnished, seeking to harness the Flame to burn the Erdtree. The Fire Giant fights to crush the champion, but the Tarnished repeatedly strikes at the Giant's legs, slicing apart his leg brace and causing the Giant's left leg to break. In immense pain, the Fire Giant tears off the foot of his broken leg, using it as a sacrifice to unleash the power of the fell god. Despite being on more even terms, the Fire Giant is eventually felled by the Tarnished.

The War Against the Giants refers to the conflict between the Fire Giants and the champions of the Erdtree, long before the events of Elden Ring.

Long ago, the red-haired Fire Giants took up residence in the northern Mountaintops, chasing away the ice dragons who were the former lords of the region.[1] The Fire Giants were considered neighbors by the astrologers who had also established themselves on the mountaintops.[2]

The Giants borrowed a destructive, fiery power from a fell god, whose one-eyed visage[3] manifested upon their chests, however the cost for this was eternal servitude as keepers of the flame of ruin[4], which resided within the forge of the Giants.

Meanwhile, Queen Marika the Eternal, an Empyrean vessel of the Elden Ring, had begun to establish her reign over the Lands Between. The flame of ruin posed a threat to the burgeoning Erdtree, being capable of burning it[5], and thus needed to be neutralized. And so, Queen Marika and her consort Godfrey, First Elden Lord, marched upon the Mountaintops of the Giants.

The War Against the Giants

The war against the Giants, fought at the birth of the Erdtree[6], was led by Godfrey.[7] They marched through the western Mountaintops, carving winding paths to the summit.[8] Upon arriving in the Mountaintops, Queen Marika issued a proclamation to Godfrey and his warriors, commanding them to put the Giants to the sword and confine their flame, so that the Age of the Erdtree could begin.[9]

The heroes of the Erdtree were accompanied by the Fire Monks, who devised an incantation which could protect them from the Giants' flame.[10] They were also joined by the Knights of Zamor, who had been mortal enemies of the Fire Giants since time immemorial[11], having challenged them many times in the past.[12]

The Trolls, who were descendants of the Giants[13], betrayed their ancestors[14] and fought on behalf of the Erdtree. They were furnished with gilded swords[15] to commemorate their fealty.

The Giants retaliated, using their bellowing roars to trigger avalanches and whip up storms of flame.[16] Facing a Fire Giant was seen as a horror, thanks in part to their dreadful visages and the flames they wielded.[17] Enormous, crushing weapons were deployed to counter their onslaught[18], and the heroes of the Erdtree strengthened their arms using semi-vitrified smithing stones found in the cold, northern regions.[6]

Queen Marika herself did battle with the one-eyed fell god, and it is believed to have been slain by her.[3] In truth, the fell god continued to lurk within the Fire Giants themselves.[19] Despite the odds, the champions of the Erdtree prevailed over the Fire Giants[4], leaving the battlefield littered with their corpses.

Although the Giants had been defeated, it became apparent that the flame of ruin would never die. Seeing this, Queen Marika marked a lone surviving Fire Giant with a curse, compelling him to tend to the flame for eternity.[20] With the flame sealed away, the Fire Monks and Flame Guardians were appointed to watch over it.[21][22] They would later succumb to the allure of the flame[23], emblazoning their chestplates with depictions of the fell god.[24]

The Knights of Zamor earned great renown[25] for their actions during the war, and were hailed as heroes. They can be found in Hero's Graves, seemingly serving as guardians. The Trolls, despite their own efforts in the war, did not receive such recognition, and can often be found performing menial labour, working in mines or dragging carriages.

The end of the war marked the dawn of the era of the Erdtree[14], presided over by Queen Marika and Godfrey. The Erdtree itself would go on to become the embodiment of Order[26], its blessed sap dripping from its boughs. The age of plenty which ensued ended swiftly, however, and the Erdtree became more an object of faith.[27]

Although the flame of ruin was sealed, the burning of the Erdtree was considered to be the first cardinal sin[28]. Prophets would occasionally glimpse the flame of ruin in their faith, envisioning the ruin that it would bring.[29] Prophets who had such visions would be banished[30], forced to wear shackles around their necks to warn passersby against listening to them.[31]

Some time after The Shattering, a Tarnished would arrive in the Lands Between and meet Melina, a mysterious woman who would guide them along the path to become Elden Lord. Finding that the entrance to the Erdtree was obstructed by thorns, Melina advises the Tarnished that the only way to gain entry was to set the Erdtree aflame.[32] The pair journey to the giant's forge, where the Tarnished fights and defeats the Fire Giant whom Marika had left to tend the Flame. Melina offers herself as kindling, and sets fire to the Erdtree using the fire that had long been sealed away.

entries.name: Fell God
entries.content:
The fell god,[1] also known as the one-eyed god,[2] is an unseen character in Elden Ring. It is the source of the Giants' Flame and Giants' Flame Incantations.

The fell god is an ancient deity worshiped by the Fire Giants. It is commonly referred to with a myriad of derogatory terms by the inhabitants of the Lands Between, such as the "corrupt", "grotesque", "malformed", "fell" or "evil" god of the Fire Giants. It is represented in the visage of a single eye with a fiery-orange iris and nine pupils within.

It physically manifests itself in the shape of a grotesque face in the torsos of its followers, channeling its power through them, its greatest flames emerging from its mouth (commonly located in the host giant's stomach) along with the undying flames found seeded within their giant black forge enabling its followers to develop innumerable fire incantations.

The fell god of fire has been around for a long time and predates the Erdtree. It was a dreaded figure in the old legends of the hornsent of Enir-Ilim.[3] It was worshiped by the Fire Giants,[2] who it cursed for eternity to tend the Flame within the Forge of the Giants.[1]

The powers of the Flame were once deemed as a threat to the Erdtree by Queen Marika and the Golden Order and thus they waged a bloody War Against the Giants. Once the Fire Giants were defeated,[1] Queen Marika realized the fires of their forge could not die and thus sealed it away,[4] reducing its once formidable flame into mere embers and cursing the last surviving Fire Giant to keep them so for all eternity.[5]

Even then, after countless years, innumerable Prophets would be haunted by visions of its flames consuming the Erdtree.[6] And the one-eyed god still lurks dormant within its subjects,[7] on the cusp of being awakened at any moment with a sufficient sacrificial offering.

The Furnace Golems, One-Eyed Shield, and Fire Monk Armor were created in the image of the fell god.
The fell god was said to possess curled horns.[3]
Eight small pupils encircle the central pupil of the fell god's eye.
This distinctive pattern appears on the Divine Towers, with some pillar reliefs featuring central cavities filled with glowing meteorite ore.
The Troll's Hammer also displays the nine-circle design, used by giants during an age when smithing held divine significance.[8]
The Verdigris Discus shares this pattern with the fell god's eye. Verdigris, believed to be a gift from an outer god,[9] also appears on the talismans and great dish carried by the Fire Giant.
This pattern is also seen on the One-Eyed Shield, Furnace Visage, Verdigris Armor, and Verdigris Greaves.
The fell god’s Flame was said to cleanse the body of poison and scarlet rot.[10]
The sun medallion on the Dung Eater's Omen Armor resembles the Furnace Visage. Red hair appears to grow from the severed Omen horns.
Red hair grows on many of its followers.

entries.name: Starscourge Conflict
entries.content: The Starscourge Conflict refers the clash between General Radahn and the stars of the night sky. Commonly described as a completely one-sided battle in Radahn's favor, the conclusion of this confrontation would earn the young warrior the title of "Starscourge" (星砕きの "Hoshi-Kudaki" litterally meaning "star crusher" or "star smasher"), secure the safety of the town of sorcery, Sellia and would fetter the very movement of the stars, halting the fates they'd ordain for their subjects, which would include the fate of Lunar Princess Ranni, Radahn's own sister. From this day onward, only when Radahn has fully perished, will the stars ever dare to resume their movements.

entries.name: Alexander, Warrior Jar
entries.content:
Alexander is a living jar who travels the Lands Between, honing his strength in order to become a great warrior.[1] Alexander was created to be a warrior vessel, and the remains of many great warriors reside within him.[2] He originally came from Jarburg, a hidden village of living jars in Liurnia of the Lakes, however he vowed never to return[3], claiming that "the path of champions must be trod alone".[4]

On his journey to become a great champion, he seeks out Redmane Castle in Caelid, following rumours of a festival of combat.[5] On his way to the festival, he crosses paths with the Tarnished multiple times, often requiring their assistance to get out of unfortunate situations such as being stuck in potholes.

Alexander finally gets the chance to participate in the Radahn Festival, a brawl between several champions and Starscourge Radahn. Alexander survives the ordeal, however he suffers damage to his body and is forced to hide for the remainder of the battle.[6] Undeterred, he replenishes himself with the bodies of mighty warriors littering the battlefield, vowing to grow even stronger.[7]

Next, Alexander travels to Mt. Gelmir, hoping to temper his body in the sea of fire[8] such that it would never crack again. Finding the lava to be lukewarm and insufficient to strengthen his vessel, he sets his sights upon the Mountaintops of the Giants, seeking out the flame of ruin.[9]

Alexander travels to the mountaintops, where he witnesses the Tarnished's fight with the Fire Giant.[10] He then finds himself in Farum Azula, where he encounters the Tarnished for a final time. Impressed by his companion's feats of strength, he requests a duel[11]. The Tarnished emerges victorious and Alexander accepts his defeat, asking the Tarnished to take his innards with his final words.[12]

The Tarnished may present these innards to Alexander's nephew, the Jar-Bairn, who vows to become strong just like his uncle Alexander.[13]

entries.name: Torrent
entries.content:
Torrent is a spectral steed resembling a horse with two short horns on his head and a white mane. Prior to meeting the Tarnished, he is in the company of Melina. The pair find the Tarnished unconscious in the Stranded Graveyard, where Melina reassures Torrent[1] before granting the Tarnished two flasks. Later, when the Tarnished enters into an accord with Melina, she grants them the Spectral Steed Whistle which allows them to call upon Torrent, revealing that Torrent has chosen them.[2]

Torrent has a taste for Rowa Raisins,[3] Sweet Raisins[4] and Frozen Raisins,[5] which can be used to restore his health. He had a former master who also gave Ranni the Witch the Spirit Calling Bell to pass onto his next master.[6] The identity of this individual is not currently known.

Should the Tarnished choose to become the Lord of Frenzied Flame and incinerate the Erdtree, a final cutscene will show Melina picking up the Spectral Steed Whistle, which disintegrates in her hand (though the player still has access to it in-game).

Besides allowing a player to get around relatively quickly, Torrent also doesn't appear to take fall damage from certain heights. This allows one to easily jump down from heights that'd normally kill the player as long as they're mounted on Torrent. That said, Torrent isn't immune to dying from jumping from too high of a height: even if a double jump is used to get to a lower level, if the starting point is too high up, Torrent will dissipate on landing and the player will die from the impact.

Jumping again while in mid-air will cause Torrent to perform a second jump. This can only be done once until he touches the ground again and can be used to change direction at the moment of the second jump.

Players can also fight from horseback against enemies, such as shooting arrows or casting spells. However, only one of the player's weapons can be used at a time as the left hand is constantly occupied holding Torrent's reigns, it is still possible to switch between the right-hand and left-hand armament while riding by using the same input the player uses to two-hand their weapons.

Note that it is not possible to change from wielding a weapon one-handed to two-handed while mounted. It is however possible to get the bonuses of two-handing by performing the action before mounting up.

Spirit springs can be used by jumping while riding Torrent to reach higher altitudes. Landing on or close to a spirit spring will completely negate fall damage.

Torrent's HP can be restored by consuming Rowa Raisins, Sweet Raisins and Frozen Raisins. Using a Flask of Crimson Tears will also restore his health on top of the player's own, however only while the player is riding him. If Torrent is killed, using the Spectral Steed Whistle will bring up a prompt to expend a single charge of the Flask of Crimson Tears to revive him.

entries.name: Dung Eater
entries.content:
Background
The Dung Eater once saw guidance and a ring that would appear at the end of his journey.[1] His vision is of a curse he calls the "pox upon life itself" or the "reviled blessing",[2] with everyone sustaining it in despair and their souls not being able to return to the Erdtree.[3][4][5] He decided to wear a disfigured armor, resembling the Omen, representing the vision of the landscape of his mind, and his appearance as he wished to see it.[6] He donned his armor with a heavy sun-shaped medallion to represent both the guidance and the ring he once saw.[7]

He assumed he would personally curse all life himself, so he started indiscriminately killing people and defiling their corpses to nourish the pox.[8] In each defilement, the Dung Eater cultivates a Seedbed Curse on a corpse that prevents the dead soul to go to the Erdtree, leaving it forever cursed.[9]

He was eventually captured and publicly hanged in front of an angry crowd, who strongly despise him for his vile crimes. However, killing the Dung Eater only resulted in his revival by grace as a Tarnished,[10] so he was perpetually jailed in the Forsaken Depths below Leyndell, the Royal Capital.

When The Tarnished (Protagonist) travels to the Roundtable Hold, an apparition of the Dung Eater is discovered within, resting and with his bloodlust quenched by his abidance of the pact of non-aggression[11][12]; but should he feel the presence of his Seedbed Curse within the player, he'll instruct to set his body free from the jail hidden away in the sewer below the capital,[13] with the intention of fully cursing The Tarnished.[14]

If The Dung Eater is released, he will attack and defile Blackguard Big Boggart, and will invade the player when they arrive at the scene. When defeated, Dung Eater will claim something unexpected happened, his blessing was warded off by the protagonist, despite the curse stirring within, a feat no one had succeeded in before. [15] At which point he has a revelation: he was not the one who could curse the world as in his vision, that's The Tarnished. And the Dung Eater is just a means to get there, and should be doing what his moniker implies — his flesh is the one that must receive the blessing.[16] And so, he tasks his flesh to be defiled with the seedbed curse again and again until the ring he once saw coalesces and is able to defile Order itself,[17], an act that would cost his life but that he would be proud of.[18]

The player can choose to follow the Dung Eater's will, defiling his body unto a Mending Rune is created, and using it to bring a new age of despair in the end. The Tarnished may also choose to put a stop to his trail of blood by simply killing him in his jail, or to reduce the Dung Eater to a mindless puppet through Seluvis' Potion. Still, perhaps this is a fate too cruel even for a monster like him.

The Dung Eater’s name and methods of killing might be inspired by an ancient Japanese myth; it was once believed that a person’s soul was contained within a special organ located in the anus. Demons would tear this organ out of their victims in order to steal their souls.

entries.name: GoldMask
entries.content:
Goldmask is a Tarnished scholar and staunch Golden Order fundamentalist.[1] He predicted the guidance of Grace, and upon being beckoned by it he came to the Lands Between to contemplate the Golden Order.[2]

Although a Golden Order fundamentalist himself, Goldmask was critical of the hunters of Those Who Live in Death, lamenting that their learnedness had been reduced to fanatical raving and an obsession with finding a great evil to contend with, a concept which he did not believe existed within the Golden Order.[3]

While contemplating the Erdtree in the Altus Plateau Goldmask is approached by Brother Corhyn, a man of the cloth who wished to travel alongside him as a scholar. In Leyndell, Goldmask becomes perplexed by the identity of Radagon, whose existence calls into question the principle that Queen Marika the Eternal is the one true god.[4] With the help of the The Tarnished, Goldmask learns that Radagon is Marika.

Goldmask and Corhyn then travel to the Mountaintops of the Giants, where Corhyn becomes aware of Goldmask's suspicions regarding the holism of the Golden Order.[5] Corhyn begins to doubt Goldmask's faith, questioning his decision to travel to the Mountaintops.[6]

Goldmask had come to the revelation that the imperfection of the Golden Order and the instability of ideology was due to the fickleness of the gods.[7] After the Erdtree burns, Goldmask returns to Leyndell and dies on the hill near the Erdtree Sanctuary, leaving behind the Mending Rune of Perfect Order, which would allow the Golden Order to be perfected.

Goldmask is among the Tarnished listed in the game's intro. He is depicted splayed on the ground across a carving of the Erdtree Incantation sigil, alongside a book and a container leaking a golden fluid. Grace can be seen gleaming in front of him.

entries.name: Miriel, Pastor of Vows
entries.content:
Miriel, Pastor of Vows is the steward of the Church of Vows in eastern Liurnia of the Lakes. A gigantic tortoise wearing a large white mitre, Miriel is a gentle soul who will happily assist The Tarnished on their journey.

Well-versed in both sorceries and incantations, Miriel can be given scrolls as well as prayerbooks, and will readily teach new spells to the player for an appropriate fee.

Miriel also serves as an excellent source of lore on Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon, and her former husband, Radagon of the Golden Order. Exhausting Miriel's dialogue can direct the player toward secrets that advance multiple questlines.

Miriel is the most reliable cleric NPC for prayerbooks, since he never moves away from the church, accepts all types of books and only becomes unavailable once during the Bell Bearing Hunter invasion.

entries.name: Crumbling Farum Azula
entries.content:
Crumbling Farum Azula is a subregion of the Lands Between in Elden Ring. This legacy dungeon is accessible after burning the Erdtree at the Forge of the Giants found on Flame Peak in the Mountaintops of the Giants.

A giant temple in the sky, located above the sea to the east of the Lands Between. Once a royal city and the seat of the Dragonlord Placidusax, Farum Azula has been crumbling since time immemorial.[1] Now, it is a mausoleum, guarded by chosen Beastmen who wield weapons clad in lightning.[2] The storm beyond time rages in the center of the crumbling city, and at its heart is the Dragonlord's seat, where he awaits the return of his god.[3]

As well as Beastmen, Farum Azula is home to a number of Ancient Dragons, who roost on the floating fragments of the city. There is also a population of Wormfaces dwelling in one of the lower levels of the city. It appears that Deathroot has spread throughout parts of the city as well.

Farum Azula is the dwelling place of Maliketh, the Black Blade, the protector of the Rune of Death. It is here that the Tarnished finds themselves after the Erdtree is set aflame, and where they finally unbind the Rune of Death, releasing it upon the Lands Between.

entries.name: DragonLord Placidusax
entries.content:
Dragonlord Placidusax is a boss in Elden Ring, encountered in Crumbling Farum Azula.

In the prehistoric era before the age of the Erdtree, the world was ruled by the Ancient Dragons[1]. Above them all was Placidusax, a many-headed Ancient Dragon who ruled as Elden Lord[2] from the royal city of Farum Azula.[3]

At some point, Placiudsax was betrayed by one of his own; Bayle the Dread. Bayle inflicted a grievous wound upon the Dragonlord before fleeing, eventually coming to reside in the Realm of Shadow. Placidusax had his servants shephard the humans into hunting Bayle and his brood, the drakes, laying the foundations of Dragon Communion.[4]

When Placidusax's god fled, the Dragonlord resolved to await its return, withdrawing to his seat at the heart of the storm beyond time.[2] Farum Azula became a mausoleum enshrining Placidusax, guarded by chosen Beastmen.[5] In his absence, the age of the Erdtree began under the rule of Queen Marika the Eternal, and the descendants of the Ancient Dragons became enfeebled, weak to the primeval lightning wielded by their forebears.[6][7] Placidusax's Gravel Stone Scales were disseminated throughout the world, used as smithing stones said to allow for the creation of god-slaying weapons by lightly twisting time.[8]

Despite his stasis, Placidusax continued to grant blessings to his followers.[9]

A Tarnished eventually finds their way into Placidusax's seat at the heart of the storm while exploring Farum Azula in search of the Rune of Death. They approach Placidusax, who attempts to ward off the intruder. Placidusax ultimately falls to the Tarnished interloper, dying without ever being reunited with their missing god.

Placidusax shows serious signs of damage on it's body. Notably he is missing three of his five heads and second pair of wings, in spite of the Old Lord's Talisman showing just four with complete wings.[10]

Two of the Dragonlord's lost heads, as well as parts of their respective necks, can be found on the body of Bayle the Dread, still biting into the drake's neck.

Part of a dragon’s body (an arm, wing, and head) resembling Placidusax can be seen sticking out of a body of rock in Farum Azula prior to reaching his arena.
According to the Remembrance of the Dragonlord, Placidusax was an Elden Lord before the era of the Erdtree, making him the earliest known Elden Lord.
Placidusax's design is most likely modeled after King Ghidorah.

entries.name: Ancient Dragons
entries.content:
The Ancient Dragons ruled in the prehistoric era before the Erdtree.[1] They wielded red lightning as a weapon[2], and had scales made of sharp, pointed gravel stones.[3] They were ruled over by Dragonlord Placidusax, said to have been Elden Lord in the time before the Erdtree[4], from the royal city of Farum Azula[5], and it is said that they would protect their lord as a wall of living rock.[6]

Ancient Dragons have light grey bodies resembling stone. They possess four legs, as well as four wings inlayed with gold, distinguishing them from their lesser descendants. They have short, flat muzzles, orange-yellow eyes, and wispy grey hairs along their backs. They can breathe fire like many of their descendants, however they also possess the ability to wield red lightning, which often manifests in the form of spears and glaives.

During the reign of Queen Marika the Eternal, the Ancient Dragon Gransax wrought havoc on Leyndell, Royal Capital, the only time in recorded history that Leyndell's walls have fallen.[7] This marked the dawn of the war against the Dragons, during which the Tree Sentinels clad themselves in armour resembling the bodies of the Dragons in order to protect the Erdtree.[8] During this conflict Godwyn the Golden fought to the last against the Ancient Dragon Fortissax.[9] Godwyn defeated Fortissax, however he befriended his fallen foe, ending the conflict and giving rise to the capital's Ancient Dragon Cult.[10] Worship of the Ancient Dragons does not conflict with faith in the Erdtree, as the Dragons' lightning is imbued with gold, and as such the Cult was permitted within Leyndell.[11]

entries.name: Bayle The Dread
entries.content:
Bayle the Dread was a legendary black dragon who is said to be the ancestor of the drakes or lesser dragons. Long ago, Bayle betrayed the Ancient dragons and clashed with Dragonlord Placidusax.[1] Their vicious battle ended in stalemate and left both dragons with grievous injuries and loss of body parts, with Bayle losing his two winged arms, his pair of wings on his back and his left leg, with the dreaded dragon fleeing to the Jagged Peak soon afterwards.[2][3]

Dragon Communion
As punishment for his betrayal, Placidusax created the art of Dragon Communion, sending his followers to shepherd humanity into hunting Bayle and his descendants.[4] As reward for felling the drakes, the dragon hunters consumed their hearts in order to gain their power. Bayle was pursued by Florissax, a servant of Placidusax who sought to recruit mortals in the hunt for Bayle.[5][6]

Dragonslayer Igon, a particularly obsessive drake warrior, was one such mortal. Igon faced Bayle, but was left broken in both body and spirit by their battle.[7][8]

Igon was stumbled upon by a Tarnished champion, and begged them to summon his spirit to face Bayle once more. Together, the pair succeed in slaying Bayle.[9][10]

If Bayle's heart eaten at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion, his willpower will one day consume the body and soul of the drake warrior.[11]

entries.name: Dragon Communion
entries.content:
Dragon Communion (竜餐, Ryūsan) is a historical practice in Elden Ring. It involves the hunting of drakes, the descendants of Ancient Dragons, in pursuit of their gravel stone-covered hearts.

Specifically, Dragon Communion is the act of consuming dragon hearts in order to acquire the draconic powers within. The hearts are consumed at a Dragon Communion Altar which is usually in the presence of a fallen dragon.

In the distant past, the lord of the ancient dragons, Placidusax, was attacked by the great drake, Bayle the Dread. Their clash ended in a stalemate and left both gravely injured, with Bayle fleeing the field of battle. As vengeance for Bayle's transgression, Placidusax had some of his followers take mortal forms as humanoid priestesses and travel to the lands of men, where they would beckon human warriors to their cause. They established the practice of dragon communion in order to hunt down and punish Bayle and his descendants, the drakes. The human warriors were lured to this cause with the promise of great power which could only be acquired by consuming the heart of a drake.[citation needed]

As time passed, the practice would continue without influence from the priestesses, however many practitioners would forget the original purpose of these hunts and would simply carry on consuming hearts in pursuit of personal gain. Some drakes have become aware of this practice, such as Ekzykes the Decaying, who even after succumbing to Malenia's rot would never forget his hatred and thus keeps himself stationed at the entrance of the Cathedral of Dragon Communion, so that he may kill or deter any would-be practitioners before they can reach the altar.[citation needed]

Many practicioners develop a hunger for the hearts as they hunt, which becomes gradually intensifies the more hearts they devour. This leads many to commune without restraint, an act that has dire consequences for their humanity, as their bodies and minds gradually become more and more draconic. The end-result is transformation into Magma Wyrms, dragon-like creatures with pitifully small wings, incapable of flight and cursed to crawl the earth on their bellies until the end of their days. Ironically, this end often comes at the hands of their fellow communers as their own hearts are now a sufficient target for dragon communion as well.

entries.name: Grandmother
entries.content:
The Grandmother is an unseen character in Shadow of the Erdtree. A statue in her image can be found inside a tree at the Shaman Village in the Hinterland.

The Grandmother was important to the residents of the Shaman Village.[1] Marika left a Golden Braid as an offering to the Grandmother.

The Grandmother is the statue of a maiden with eyes obscured by long silver hair worn in two distinct braids. Her features strongly resemble those of the shaman Jar Innards. A stone dress clings to her emaciated frame. She is found encased within a hollow tree trunk. Roots or branches of the tree appear to be reaching toward her.

The headless statue found outside Bonny Village resembles the Grandmother.
The Grandmother may have embedded herself into the tree to water it with her blood in the way Miquella did his Haligtree.

entries.name: Shaman Village
entries.content:
Shaman Village is a Location in Elden Ring, added with the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC. It is revealed to be the hometown of Queen Marika, The Eternal, the current ruler of the Lands Between. The village is found in the Scaduview region, a hidden area that is unlocked by using the "O Mother" gesture on a statue of Marika nearby the Shadow Keep, Back Gate Site of Grace.

Cite: "Marika bathed the village of her home in gold, knowing full well that there was no one to heal. What was her prayer? Her wish, her confession? There is no one left to answer, and Marika never returned home again."

entries.name: Gate of Divinity
entries.content:
Gate of Divinity is a mysterious place atop of Enir-Ilim that seemingly allows ascension to godhood. It is a location in Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree.

The Gate of Divinity has seemingly existed since time immemorial.

Before the Age of the Erdtree, an Empyrean and Numen woman hailing from the Shaman Village named Marika traveled to the Gate and ascended to godhood. There she became the vessel of the Elden Ring. Her ascension led to the creation of the Erdtree and the Scadutree and ushered in a new era, with Marika becoming sovereign of the Lands Between and Godfrey becoming her spouse and the first Elden Lord.

Following the death of Mohg, Lord of Blood, his corpse was stolen and transported to the Land of Shadow where Miquella would require it for an ancient ritual. At the Gate of Divinity Miquella ascended to godhood and resurrected Radahn, using the body of Mogh as a vessel. Miquella then blessed Radahn and made him his consort. The Tarnished then defeats Radahn and Miquella, preventing the latter's "Age of Compassion".

If struck with a weapon, the Gate of Divinity bleeds.
The Gate appears to have ropes on it.[1]

entries.name: Empyreans
entries.content:
Empyreans (神人, Shinjin) are special beings that are capable of becoming gods of a new age[1] and forging a new order that governs the world.[2] One such way in which they can achieve this is by becoming the vessel of the Elden Ring.

The most prominent Empyrean is Queen Marika, a Numen who became the vessel of the Elden Ring and founded the Golden Order.

At least during the reign of Marika, Empyreans were chosen by the Two Fingers.[3] Each Empyrean typically will chose consort either before or after their assention to godhood, who are themselves themselves is award the title of lord.

The Two Fingers were known to grant Empyreans a shadowbound beast upon their selection, sometimes simply refered to as "shadows", to serve as loyal vassals.[4] Though incapable of treachery towards their Empyrean, should their master resist the will of the Two Fingers, they will decend into maddness, becoming a curse rather than a protecter.[5] The only two shadowbound beasts currently known are Maliketh, who serves Marika, and Blaidd, who serves Ranni. Whether all Empyreans are granted a shadow is unclear, as there is no concrete evidence to discount either side.

The only other Empyrean known from a time before the Golden Order was the Gloam-Eyed Queen, who had been a rival candidate for godhood alongside Marika herself. Markia's vision for a new age demanded the removal of the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring. This was an affront to the Gloam-Eyed Queen, who's power stemmed from the Rune of Death in the form of the Black Flame. On behalf of Marika, the Gloam-Eyed Queen was slain in battle by her shadow, Maliketh. Afterwards, Marika extracted the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring. She gave it to Maliketh to protect, having it bound to his sword. With the Gloam-Eyed Queen dead, and the Rune of Death imprisoned, the power of the Black Flame was weakened exponentially.

During the Age of the Erdtree, three Empyrean were named as Marika's potential successors: Miquella, Malenia and Ranni.[6] Miquella and Malenia were twins born of a single god, being children of both Markia, and her second husband Radagon, a champion created from Marika's own being. Their powerful lineage is indicated to be the reason why that they were prime candidates for Empyrean.[7] Ranni was the daughter of Radagon and his previous wife before Marika, Queen Rennala of the Full Moon. This confirms that being the child of full gods is not a strict requirement to be an Empyrean, as Ranni herself was only a demigod.

Miquella himself was almost able to ascend to godhood and bring about his envisioned "Age of Compassion", but was stopped and slain in battle by the Tarnished. Unlike her brother, Malenia would briefly ascend to godhood as the Goddess of Rot during her battle with the same Tarnished warrior, but was similarly defeated.[8]. As for Ranni, she has the potential to bring about her Age of Stars with the assistance of the Tarnished, who she makes her consort.[9] The Tarnished can become Marika's third consort, using her imprisoned form to bring about the Ages of Fracture, Order, Duskborn or introduce the Blessing of Despair.[10]

List of Empyrean: 
Queen Marika the Eternal[11]
Ranni the Witch[1]
Malenia, Blade of Miquella[1]
Miquella of the Haligtree[1]
The Gloam-Eyed Queen

entries.name: The Gloam-Eyed Queen
entries.content:
The Gloam-Eyed Queen was an Empyrean who was defeated long ago by Maliketh. She was the leader of the Godskin Apostles and wielded the god-slaying power of Destined Death.[1][2][3]

The Gloam-Eyed Queen was an Empyrean chosen by her own Two Fingers. She led the apostles in their god hunt,[3] wielded the power of Destined Death and channeling its Black Flames through her Godslayer's Greatsword.[1] She cradled newborn Godskin Apostles in a swaddling cloth made from patches of supple skin sewn together.[4] Her apostles developed inhuman physiology and would grow to be the death of the gods.[5]

The Golden Order
Queen Marika desired the removal of the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring to create the Golden Order.[6] After the Gloam-Eyed Queen and her apostles were defeated at the hands of Maliketh, the Rune of Death was sealed away within his Black Blade and the true power of the Godslayer incantations was lost.[7][8][9] The Gloam-Eyed Queen's sword was locked away at the bottom of the Divine Tower of Caelid, and her fate remains unknown.

The Gloam-Eyed Queen's Godskin Swaddling Cloth is guarded by the summoned spirits of Godskin Apostles in Spiritcaller's Cave on the Mountaintops of the Giants.

entries.name: Game endings
entries.content:
The various endings in Elden Ring are tied to choices made by the player throughout their journey, as well as optional questlines. These outcomes define the fate of the Lands Between, and the role the Tarnished assumes as Queen Marika's Elden Lord or otherwise. Each ending represents the Tarnished brandishing the Elden Ring and ushering in their new Age.

Note: Receiving the Flame of Frenzy from the Three Fingers in the Frenzied Flame Proscription will lock the player out of all endings except the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending. This restriction can be lifted by using Miquella's Needle when prompted at Dragonlord Placidusax's boss arena, however, doing so will permanently lock the player out of the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending.

Choosing an Ending
After defeating the final boss, the Tarnished will return to a room containing Marika's statue and a nearby Grace. If Ranni's questline has been completed, her summon sign will also appear near the Fractured Marika statue. At this point, the player can choose an ending by interacting with either Marika's statue or, if available, Ranni's summon sign.

If the Tarnished possesses the Frenzied Flame, Ranni's summon sign will not appear unless the Frenzied Flame has been removed using Miquella's Needle. In this scenario, the only option is to interact with Marika's statue, which automatically triggers the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending, offering no alternative choices.

Without the Frenzied Flame, interacting with Marika's statue presents the option to select one of three possible mending runes obtained during the Tarnished's journey. Choosing a rune initiates the corresponding ending: Age of Order, Age of the Duskborn, or Blessing of Despair. Alternatively, players can choose to "Mend the Elden Ring" without a rune, resulting in the Age of Fracture ending.

If Ranni's summon sign is present and selected instead of Marika's statue, the Age of the Stars ending will begin.

Regardless of the choice, the nearby Site of Grace allows the player to teleport elsewhere and return later, postponing the ending and enabling continued exploration.

To start a New Game Plus, an ending must be selected. After the end credits, players can choose "Begin Journey X" or return later to the Roundtable Hold Grace to initiate the new playthrough.

Elden Lord
The Age of Fracture, Age of Order, Age of the Duskborn, and Blessing of Despair endings all result in the Tarnished becoming Marika's new Elden Lord. Each offers a different interpretation of Marika's vision for the Golden Order, mending the Elden Ring and ushering in their new Age of choice to rule over.

Age of Fracture
In the Age of Fracture ending, the Tarnished becomes Elden Lord without adding any special Mending Runes to the Elden Ring. In doing so, they fulfill the Two Fingers' plans of using the Tarnished to restore the sense of stability not felt since the Elden Ring was shattered. The Golden Order remains in the truest state possible to what it once was and the status quo is restored.

Age of Order
The Tarnished becomes Elden Lord, fulfilling Goldmask's idea of a "Perfect" Golden Order based on his research into how it had fallen to its current state. Realizing that the Golden Order's imperfections stemmed from the fickleness of the gods, who, in fact, were no better than men, Goldmask's new transcendental ideology attempts to bring true Age of Order to the Lands Between.

Age of the Duskborn
The Tarnished becomes Elden Lord, wielding the rune born from Fia and the Prince of Death's union. Just as the Golden Order had been created by confining Rune of Death, the Tarnished creates a new order of death restored. The principle of life in death is embedded within this order, and Those Who Live in Death are allowed to live in peace. Thus begins the Age of the Duskborn.


Blessing of Despair
The Tarnished becomes Elden Lord, bringing about an accursed world where defilement becomes the norm. All will become cursed in the Blessing of Despair ending. Thus, none can be scorned, fulfilling the Dung Eater's twisted vision.

Age of the Stars

The Age of the Stars ending sees The Tarnished aid Ranni the Witch in ousting Marika and remaining at her side as Ranni's first Elden Lord.

The Tarnished helps Ranni fulfill her vision of a Lands Between without the Golden Order by allowing her to replace Marika in godhood and take the role of her consort. Ranni ushers in a new order not of gold, but of the stars and moon of the chill night. Rather than make herself and her order objects of worship, she chooses instead to keep her order and the Lands Between at a great divide, removing the certainties that had existed during Marika's rule.

The Tarnished and Ranni leave the Lands Between, embarking on a thousand-year voyage into darkness under the wisdom of the Moon.

Lord of Frenzied Flame
The Lord of Frenzied Flame ending, caused by the possession of the Frenzied Flame, overrides the possibility of any other ending. The Tarnished disregard the notion of becoming Elden Lord, becoming the Lord of Frenzied Flame instead and incinerating everything that came before.

Rather than become Elden Lord, The Tarnished becomes the Lord of Frenzied Flame, fulfilling the machinations of Shabriri, and the Three Fingers's will. The Tarnished is left almost completely alone, the Frenzied Flame rapidly consuming everything in existence.

If Melina was not sacrificed, she is seen vowing to hunt down and kill the Tarnished for not heeding her earlier warnings. For The Tarnished to separate themselves from the Frenzied Flame's influence after being inherited, they must acquire Miquella's Needle and follow its specific conditions of use. Once the Frenzied Flame is suppressed, it can not be reclaimed in any way, preventing the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending.


The Age of Fracture is the simplest to obtain, only requiring the player to finish the game, while all others demand completion of their respective side quests beforehand.
The Lord of Frenzied Flame ending has an additional bonus ending cutscene if Melina was not sacrificed as a maiden. It shows her finding the burned Spectral Steed Whistle in the ashen ground and stating that she will now follow through with her vow to kill The Tarnished with Destined Death for becoming the Lord of Frenzied Flame.
If Melina was sacrificed and The Tarnished became the Lord of Frenzied Flame afterward, the bonus cutscene would simply not play.
Trivia
An unused variant of the Age of Order ending was titled the Age Absolute.[1]
The Age of Fracture has an unused alternate introduction.[2]
Among the cut content surrounding Miquella the Kind, there was at one point an ending associated with him. Miquella would have offered his dew to the Tarnished and requested their share in his dream.[3] He would have a world where "all things will flourish, whether graceful, or malign."[4] This may imply that this version of Miquella envisioned a world where even marginalized groups, such as Albinaurics and Misbegotten, would thrive.
The term "malign" in the English translation does not perfectly align with the Japanese text, which is translated literally as "not-so-graceful."
The English dialogue for the Age of the Stars ending has been debated for its interpretative differences compared to the Japanese script. Some suggest that a more literal translation may provide additional clarity, as discussed here.
